method:
Empirical trade pricing (audit 8.1 / evaluation table "Trades"): what real NHL trades looked like, valued with only what
was known on the trade date, as a check on the site's pricing rules.

Ex-ante value of each asset (no hindsight):
    prospect (no NHL games yet) his draft slot's round value (below) two years out; undrafted = 5th round
    player  WAR-lite per 82 from the three COMPLETED seasons before the trade (1 / 0.7 / 0.45 by games, 25 replacement
            games mixed in), aged with the site's growth/decline table, over a 3-season horizon: the rest of this season
            (share of the regular season left on the trade date) + the next two at x0.9 a year. Contracts weren't
            archived, so term and cap hit are ignored (a stated limitation).
    pick    the round's average 7-season WAR for drafted players (models/trades.json round_ev) x 0.9 per year until the
            draft + 2 (development); conditional picks at 70%
Per trade side: given = sum of its assets out, got = sum of assets in (only trades with every player matched to stats).
reading: Sellers' return relative to the ex-ante value they gave up; the site's rule needs package >= price x premium and a 65% headliner. Where real deals settle well below 1.0, sellers accept less than face value (scouting views, contracts, cap and fit the public value misses), so a rule demanding >= 1.0 is stricter than the market.
